Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 9, 2025
Review Body: I'm a huge fan of reading about current and past presidents, first ladies, and the White House, so when I saw Melania Trump had a new book out, I knew I wanted to read it. Plus, the cover drew me in immediately when I saw it at the bookstore, which is kind of odd because it's so simple. The book itself is an easy read that is engaging and sounds authentic. Melania has a great love for her family, she's a dedicated wife and mother that has led a fascinating and inspiring life. She talks a lot about the pitfalls and rewards of being in the public eye, she also is frank about mistakes she has made. My favorite part of the book was the super secret flight that she and President Trump took to Iraq, and then Germany, to surprise the troops on Christmas Day. The description of the trip gave me goosebumps.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 5, 2025
Review Body: I'm giving this book four stars because it was not difficult to read mechanically, but it did not hold my interest. I personally think Melania Trump is quite beautiful and elegant and gets a lot of grief just because her husband is President. I enjoy how much she loves her son, but otherwise, I found her hard to relate to. Maybe I missed it, but it's like she hasn't really had any major problems that humanize her for us plebeians. She grew up affluent in a time and place that as an American, we had been told was a horrible place to live, and she even states that the proximity of her home to Italy afforded them a lot more leeway. She speaks of her talents (being beautiful and photogenic) and her hard work (being handpicked for runway and photo modeling). I just feel like I may have learned a little bit about the events in her life, but I didn't learn anything about any life lessons she's overcome, which is what I expect from a memoir. There's a pictorial segment in the middle of the book which is nice to be able to visualize major events for her.

Review Body:
From a man's perspective who was speculative of Melina.

Beginning of book was a little slow and felt like it started flat. Quick read - finished it in about 3 hours - highlighted sections that were important and new info to me.

Enjoyed learning about her upbrining and where she is from + the social economic issues she faced from her home country. She also left communism for the American dream.

Melina is a great representation of the American dream from not just 1st and 2nd generation immigrants to America, but also Americans themselves.

I didn't enjoy the first half of book, but couldn't put the book down once I was about 1/3 through it. Maybe the same feedback would not come from a female reader - take that into consideration.

She definitely fell for a few traps and tried to outsmart the media, but it backfired continuously - interesting to hear how this impacted her family and protecting her child.

Interesting to hear that Melina and Trump don't agree on all politics but they opening communicate their feelings and do their best to understand one anothers perspective.

Donald was always supportive of Melina's passion for helping children and young education - that was great to read and their relationship is very much respected between the two.

Motherly love - so clear to me how much she cares about her son. It's very touching reading this from a man's perspective, who is also a son of a mother.

Worth the price and a great read.

Review Body:
Before getting to the content, I'd like to address some of the utterly illogical comments in some reviews about there being some type of "smudges" on the book's cover. By the way, there were none on mine, but a book's physical condition should in no way affect its rating. Would they have given The Great Gatsby a mere two stars if their copy arrived with pizza stains on it?

As for Melania's book, it is very real. It authentically captures her persona. Image and appearance are important to her. She isn't uncomfortable about discussing her lavish gowns for big events. She's not embarrassed about discussing her days as a model and how people commented on her beauty.

She tells us that she and the president love music and how he pulls her in for a dance when it's played. She talks about their courtship.

I ranked it just shy of five stars because she could have addressed Trump's numerous alleged extramarital affairs. By completing leaving them out, it seems like more of a campaign ad. Even though compared to others in the political spectrum, this is not pretentious drivel.

It's a good perspective of the Trump Administration Not extremely insightful, not riveting. Not a page-turner. But very respectable.

Review Body:
The book was a very quick, easy read which I appreciate since I don’t ever seem to have enough time these days. I was amazed at the amount of work expected of the first lady. I particularly enjoyed reading of the encounters with foreign dignitaries and the amount of research to determine proper protocol.

There were moments of pure joy as when Melania described her love for her son and some stories that made me laugh. But the
description of the FBI raid made me angry. The actions resulting from obvious political bias in the federal government is disgusting and needs to stop.

Criticizing the name of the Be Best initiative is petty. I love the simplicity of the name and the positive, important work being done under this program. Sure it could have been more gramatically acceptable, for example, Be Better. But why settle for simply being better when you can Be Best!

As far as negatives, I wanted to learn more about Melania’s early life and less about her gown selections. The attention to the world of fashion was necessary as that is such a huge part of her life. But I felt the repeated mention of top fashion designers while in the White House emphasized the huge divide between those that have “it” and those that do not.
